summary.text: Mountain building is the work of a variety of geological processes linked to large-scale movements of Earth's tectonic plates.
Folding, faulting, volcanic activity, igneous intrusion and metamorphism can all play a part, giving five main types: volcanic, fold, plateau, fault-block and dome mountains.
Volcanic arcs rise where an ocean plate meets a continent, while folding builds ranges where two continental plates meet.

facts.label: Main mountain types
facts.value: Volcanic, fold, plateau, fault-block and dome

facts.label: Older explanation
facts.value: Geosyncline theory, replaced by plate tectonics in the 1960s

facts.label: Raised fault blocks
facts.value: Called horsts; the troughs are grabens

items.prompt: A volcano keeps pouring out runny, low-viscosity basalt lava. What kind of mountain does it most likely build?

options.label: A steep cone with slopes near 35°
A broad cone with gentle slopes
A long ridge of folded rock
A tilted block lifted along a fault

items.explain: Runny basalt spreads far before it sets, so it builds a gently sloping shield volcano like Mauna Loa.

items.prompt: Two continental plates push into each other. What mainly raises the mountains where they meet?

options.label: A chain of volcanoes from melting ocean crust
A center block dropping between two others
The crust buckling and folding upward
A hotspot fed by a plume in the mantle

items.explain: Volcanic arcs belong to ocean-continent boundaries; where two continents meet, the crust folds into mountains.

items.prompt: Most of the world's volcanoes sit in a band that circles which ocean?

options.label: The Pacific
The Atlantic
The Indian
The Arctic

items.explain: The Pacific Ring of Fire holds most volcanoes, with a second band running from the Mediterranean across Asia.

items.prompt: A region's surface is stretched until the plate beneath it splits. What happens to the middle block?

options.label: It is pushed up into a dome
It crumples into tight folds
It melts and feeds a volcano
It drops down below its neighbours

items.explain: Pulling apart creates tensional forces, and when the plate splits the center block sinks relative to the blocks on each side.

items.prompt: An ocean plate sinks beneath another plate, and a line of volcanoes appears nearby. Why?

options.label: The plates pull apart and let magma well up
Friction heats the surface rocks until they melt
The sinking crust melts and drags water down
A hotspot happens to sit under the boundary

items.explain: Near a subduction zone the sinking oceanic crust melts and carries water down with it, feeding a volcanic arc.

items.prompt: Compared with a gently sloping shield volcano, how does a steep stratovolcano such as Mount Fuji tend to erupt?

options.label: More gently and more often
More violently and less often
Only under the sea
In the same way, just faster

items.explain: Its thicker, more viscous material builds a steeper cone, and its eruptions are more violent and less frequent.
